title: Risk-scoped Vendor Onboarding Portal + Variable Insurance Crediting Pilot
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise procurement cycles are elongated by one-size-fits-all questionnaire and insurance requests. High-touch legal review is required even for low-risk vendor classes. Goal: Create a risk-scoped onboarding flow in the vendor portal that (1) automatically classifies vendor risk tier based on answers + metadata, (2) surfaces a tailored SOC2 evidence package when available, and (3) applies a variable insurance crediting mechanism (a discount on onboarding friction and lead time) for vendors that provide attestation + insurance docs. This ticket scopes a pilot for mid-market and SMB ISVs used by Redwood customers, focusing on speeding procurement and reducing manual SRE/Legal touch time.
acceptance_criteria: Portal shows a clear three-tier risk classification (Low / Medium / High) with rationale visible to the reviewer
Automated mapping: if vendor provides SOC2 Type II report and control matrix link, classify as Low or Medium (per risk rules) and attach to vendor profile
Insurance crediting: system applies up to 25% expedited-review credit when vendor uploads certificate of insurance (COI) + insurer A/M rating >= A-; credit calculation visible in onboarding summary
Admin funnel: Legal/Finance can override risk tier and leave an explanation note; overrides recorded in audit log
Metrics: pilot reduces average procurement review time by >= 30% for participating vendors compared to baseline (measured on dashboard queries)
End-to-end demo script and stakeholder sign-off (Legal, Finance, Sales) completed for pilot cohort
tasks: Write PRD: define risk-scoring rules, COI parsing requirements, and UI states (owner: PM)
Design: mockups for portal flow and reviewer override panel (owner: DES)
Engineering: backend schema to store SOC2 artifacts, COI metadata, and computed insurance credit (owner: ENG)
Integrations: SSO access for vendor portal and secure upload bucket with virus scanning (owner: ENG)
Legal: define acceptable insurer ratings and COI fields + create contract addendum template (owner: Legal)
Analytics: dashboard template that compares time-to-approve and manual-touch counts for pilot vendors (owner: Data)
Pilot ops: recruit 20 candidate vendors from sales pipeline and notify internal stakeholders (owner: Ops)
Create rollback/playbook and SLA language for external pilot participants (owner: PM)
Run pilot for 8 weeks and collect feedback
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping call done with Legal (Marta Silva) and Finance (Ravi Shah). Legal proposed insurer A- threshold; Finance requested visibility into expected cost savings before approving credits.
2026-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Eng spike scheduled to prototype COI ingestion and a small parser for insurer name + limits. ENG-49830 created for parser work.
2026-03-02 - Marta Silva (Legal): Suggested adding a minimal attestation clause for SOC2 documents verifying date and scope; will draft addendum and link it to vendor portal acceptance step.

2026-03-05 - Design review: DES-2119 uploaded mockups to Figma (link below). Feedback: make rationale for automated tiering visible in the reviewer panel; surface scoring contributors (answers, SOC2 present, insurer rating).

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Proposed trade-off: start pilot without automated insurer rating lookup (manual verification) to reduce integration scope, then add lookup via third-party vendor in phase 2.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Approved phased approach. Phase 1 = automated SOC2 detection + manual COI verification + visible credit calculation. Phase 2 = insurer lookup, auto-credit issuance, and self-service appeals.
decisions: Phase 1 scope narrowed to: SOC2 artifact ingestion + manual COI verification + visible credit calculation. Removes insurer lookup to meet Q2 timeline.
Insurance credit capped at 25% for pilot to limit financial exposure; Finance will review after pilot and propose tiered caps.
Audit log entries must include original vendor-uploaded file hash and reviewer override note to satisfy compliance and incident reconstruction needs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Vendors upload forged SOC2 artifacts. Mitigation: require document metadata (issuer, date) and manual spot-checks by Legal; flag mismatches for escalation.
Risk: COI parsing errors lead to incorrect credits. Mitigation: manual verification step and conservative default (no credit) on parsing failure.
Risk: Pilot vendors decline to participate due to perceived extra work. Mitigation: Sales to offer onboarding credits and faster SLA to incentivize participation.
Risk: Security review delays launch. Mitigation: early engagement with Security (owner listed) and limited-scope storage with short retention for pilot documents.
metrics_and_dashboards: Primary: median procurement review time (days) for pilot vendors vs baseline cohort
Secondary: # of manual legal touches per vendor; % of vendors accepted with automated low-risk classification; average credit applied per vendor
Operational: parser failure rate; time-to-override for reviewer actions
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize PRD, design mocks, and Legal addendum
Week 3-6: engineering build (SOC2 ingestion API, admin UI, credit calc), analytics wiring
Week 7: internal dry-run with Legal and Finance using synthetic vendors
Week 8-15: pilot with 20 live vendors, weekly syncs and data collection
Week 16: review results, decision to iterate/scale or sunset pilot
notes: Try to keep vendor-facing scaffolding minimal to avoid scaring customers; primary improvements should be on the reviewer/admin side.
Consider later integration with Redwood Console to expose vendor-level risk and credit history for internal product teams.
